artifact: Arabic sentence bank editorial audit summary

critical_examples.issue: ترون means 'you see' while English says 'What do you think?'
Target asks 'Do you need help?' while English says 'May I help you?'
Target lacks the negation in English 'Shouldn't you go home?'
الغذاء means food/nourishment; English requires lunch (الغداء).
الفاتورة is bill/invoice; English says receipt.
تجاهل means ignore while English says fail to notice.
الصبيان means boys while English says babies.
Target expresses ability to eat, not financial affordability.
Target says crab while English says carp.
Target says look at while English says look for.
Target says look at while English says look for.
Target asks where speaker sewed the suit; English asks where they had it made.
Arabic is first-person singular 'I can'; English is first-person plural 'we can'.
Target asks why speaker cannot leave their room; English asks why they cannot have their own room.
Target says the person did not want to come; English says the person would never come.
Target asks about degree/certificate; English asks about college major.
ظهرًا is noon while English says afternoon.
Target says how much the speaker worried; English says how worried the other person made the speaker.
Arabic modality does not correctly express English 'shouldn't'.
Target says what I want to do; English says what I want you to do.
Arabic is a yes/no habitual question; English asks frequency ('How often').
Target construction هل يوجد أين is ungrammatical for the intended meaning.
Target says became a member; English says registered.
Target contains a malformed relative/person construction and requires rewriting.

root_cause: The current sentence builder validates source licensing, script plausibility, target uniqueness, and length, then ranks primarily from English-side usefulness. It does not validate Arabic grammar, spelling, MSA register, or bilingual semantic equivalence before selecting the top 1000.
release_requirements: Convert confirmed findings into a source-locked curated correction/replacement layer.
Second-pass verify every proposed correction and all native-judgment rows.
Regenerate Arabic sentence CSV and all sentence-bearing PDFs together from the curated layer.
Run deterministic structural and render regression QA after regeneration.
Complete independent native/editorial review before any absolute correctness claim.
